region.name: Northern Alaska
region.setting: Arctic tundra and permafrost: the North Slope and the Brooks Range, with a strip of interior Alaska to the south and a little of the Arctic Ocean.

variable.name: Root-zone soil wetness
variable.definition: How full of water the top meter of soil is: 0 is completely dry, 1 is saturated.

verdict.title: Possible rising trend: the two tests disagree
verdict.text: Over 1981-2025 the estimated change is +0.0136 fraction (0-1) per decade. One of the two significance tests passes and the other does not, so treat this as suggestive rather than established.

crosscheck.label: No second dataset checked
crosscheck.text: This result has not been compared with an independent dataset. It describes this dataset; whether another record would show the same is not known.

source.dataset: MERRA-2 (Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2)
source.producer: NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO)
source.access: NASA POWER Monthly and Annual API (NASA Langley Research Center)
source.kind: Reanalysis: a global model constrained by satellite and ground observations. Values are model-based estimates, not direct instrument readings.
source.caveat: MERRA-2 is a reanalysis: a model constrained by satellite and ground observations, not a direct measurement. Changes in the observing system over time (new satellites, fewer rain gauges) can create or hide trends, especially for precipitation and soil wetness. Check important results against an independent dataset.
